claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 3 years old and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I'm eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex, who is 3 years old and living with you.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand your residency and work situation. Let me ask:

**What is your current residency status in the UK? Are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen and I live here in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. It's good to know you're a British citizen living in the UK.

Now I need to understand your income situation, as this can affect Child Benefit eligibility:

**What is your approximate annual household income? Specifically, do you or your partner (if you have one) earn over £50,000 per year?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I earn around £35,000 a year, and I don't have a partner - it's just me and Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

I have one more important question to complete the assessment:

**Have you claimed Child Benefit before, or is this your first time claiming? Also, has Alex been in the UK continuously since birth, or have there been any periods where he's been outside the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This is my first time claiming - I hadn't gotten around to it before. And yes, Alex has been in the UK since he was born. He's never been outside the country.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review your circumstances:
- You are a British citizen living in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex is your 3-year-old son living with you
- Alex has been in the UK continuously since birth
- Your annual income is approximately £35,000
- This is your first claim for Child Benefit

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you meet all the key requirements:
- You are a British citizen with settled status in the UK
- Alex is under 16 years old
- Alex is living with you as a dependent child
- Your income is below the High Income Child Benefit Charge threshold
- There are no issues with Alex's residency or time spent outside the UK

You should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. I'd recommend contacting HMRC or visiting the UK government's Child Benefit page to submit your claim.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on my assessment, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**. 

All the eligibility criteria are met in your case. I'd recommend getting in touch with HMRC to submit your claim whenever you're ready. Congratulations, and best of luck with your application!
